odisha.name: Dalma
odisha.blurb: Toor dal simmered with raw papaya, pumpkin, plantain and eggplant, finished with a panch phoron tempering and served at home and in Puri's temple kitchens.

odisha.name: Pakhala Bhata
odisha.blurb: Cooked rice soaked overnight in water, sometimes lightly fermented with curd, and eaten through the hot months with fried vegetables, badi and green chilli.

odisha.name: Machha Besara
odisha.blurb: Rohu or other river fish cooked in a sharp mustard paste with garlic and turmeric, an everyday coastal Odia curry eaten with rice.

odisha.name: Dahibara Aloodum
odisha.blurb: Soft urad dal fritters soaked in spiced, thin curd and topped with spicy potato curry, sev and onions, the signature street breakfast of Cuttack.

odisha.name: Chhena Poda
odisha.blurb: Fresh chhena kneaded with sugar and semolina and baked slowly until the outside caramelises, a sweet first made in Nayagarh and offered to Lord Jagannath.

punjab.name: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
punjab.blurb: Mustard greens slow-cooked with spinach and bathua, mashed and topped with white butter, eaten with flat maize-flour bread through the Punjabi winter.

punjab.name: Amritsari Kulcha
punjab.blurb: Flaky leavened bread stuffed with spiced potato, baked in a tandoor and served with chole and onion chutney in the lanes around Amritsar's Golden Temple.

punjab.name: Langar Dal (Maa di Dal)
punjab.blurb: Whole black urad and chana dal simmered for hours with ginger and garlic, served free to everyone at the Golden Temple's community kitchen.

punjab.name: Amritsari Fish
punjab.blurb: Freshwater fish marinated in carom seeds, chilli and gram flour batter and deep-fried, a winter evening favourite at Amritsar's roadside dhabas.

punjab.name: Pinni
punjab.blurb: Dense balls of wheat flour roasted in ghee with jaggery, almonds and edible gum, made at home in winter and handed out at weddings.

rajasthan.name: Dal Baati Churma
rajasthan.blurb: Hard wheat dumplings baked over coals and dipped in ghee, served with mixed dal and sweet crumbled churma, the classic Rajasthani festive meal.

rajasthan.name: Laal Maas
rajasthan.blurb: Mutton cooked with fiery red Mathania chillies, garlic and curd, a Rajput hunting-era dish now ordered in Jodhpur and Jaipur restaurants.

rajasthan.name: Gatte ki Sabzi
rajasthan.blurb: Steamed gram flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yogurt gravy, a desert-kitchen staple made without fresh vegetables.

rajasthan.name: Pyaaz Kachori
rajasthan.blurb: Deep-fried pastry stuffed with spiced onion filling and eaten with tamarind chutney, famously sold at Jodhpur's Rawat Mishthan Bhandar.

rajasthan.name: Ghewar
rajasthan.blurb: A disc-shaped honeycomb of fried batter soaked in sugar syrup and often topped with rabri, sold across Jaipur during Teej and Raksha Bandhan.

sikkim.name: Momos
sikkim.blurb: Steamed dumplings filled with pork, chicken or cabbage and served with fiery tomato achar, sold everywhere from MG Marg in Gangtok to roadside stalls.

sikkim.name: Phagshapa
sikkim.blurb: Strips of pork fat stewed with radish and dried chillies without oil, a traditional Sikkimese dish eaten with rice.

sikkim.name: Gundruk Soup
sikkim.blurb: A sour, warming soup of fermented and sun-dried mustard and radish greens cooked with tomato, onion and chilli.

sikkim.name: Kinema Curry
sikkim.blurb: Fermented soybeans cooked with onion, tomato and turmeric, a pungent Nepali-Sikkimese protein dish served with rice.

sikkim.name: Sel Roti
sikkim.blurb: Ring-shaped, slightly sweet bread made from ground rice batter and deep-fried, prepared for Dashain and Tihar and eaten with tea.

tamil-nadu.name: Idli with Sambar and Chutney
tamil-nadu.blurb: Steamed cakes of fermented rice and urad dal batter served with lentil-vegetable sambar and coconut chutney, the standard breakfast across the state.

tamil-nadu.name: Chettinad Chicken
tamil-nadu.blurb: Chicken cooked in a dark roasted masala of black pepper, fennel, kalpasi and dried red chillies, from the Chettiar mansions of Karaikudi.

tamil-nadu.name: Kothu Parotta
tamil-nadu.blurb: Shredded flaky parotta chopped on a hot griddle with egg, salna and meat or vegetables, its clanging a familiar night sound in Madurai.

tamil-nadu.name: Tirunelveli Halwa
tamil-nadu.blurb: Glossy wheat halwa slow-cooked with ghee and sugar, famously sold hot from Iruttu Kadai near the Nellaiappar temple.

tamil-nadu.name: Palani Panchamirtham
tamil-nadu.blurb: A thick temple offering of banana, jaggery, ghee, honey and cardamom, prepared at the Murugan temple in Palani and taken home by pilgrims.

telangana.name: Hyderabadi Biryani
telangana.blurb: Basmati rice layered with marinated mutton or chicken, saffron and fried onions and cooked dum style in a sealed pot, the city's signature dish.

telangana.name: Haleem
telangana.blurb: Wheat, lentils and meat pounded together over hours into a thick, spiced porridge, sold from Hyderabad's bhattis every Ramzan.

telangana.name: Sarva Pindi
telangana.blurb: A savoury rice-flour pancake with chana dal, peanuts, sesame and curry leaves, pressed into a pan by hand, a Telangana teatime snack.

telangana.name: Bagara Baingan
telangana.blurb: Small eggplants cooked in a gravy of roasted peanuts, sesame, coconut and tamarind, the traditional side to biryani at Hyderabadi weddings.

telangana.name: Qubani ka Meetha
telangana.blurb: Dried apricots stewed down into a thick sweet and served with cream or custard, a Deccani dessert found at weddings and Nizami restaurants.

tripura.name: Mui Borok
tripura.blurb: The umbrella name for Tripuri tribal cooking, built around berma (dried fermented fish) with bamboo shoot, vegetables and very little oil.

tripura.name: Wahan Mosdeng
tripura.blurb: Boiled or grilled pork tossed with onion, roasted green chilli and herbs, a spicy salad-style dish of the Tripuri community.

tripura.name: Gudok
tripura.blurb: A thick stew of jackfruit, bamboo shoot or other vegetables cooked with berma and chillies inside a bamboo tube or pot.

tripura.name: Bangwi
tripura.blurb: Aromatic local rice wrapped in sabai leaves with ginger, onion and ghee, then boiled, made for festivals and family gatherings.

tripura.name: Chakhwi
tripura.blurb: Bamboo shoot and vegetables cooked with a little rice flour and soda from banana-plant ash, often with pork or berma added for feasts.

uttar-pradesh.name: Galouti Kebab
uttar-pradesh.blurb: Finely minced mutton blended with papaya and spices into patties so soft they melt, created for the Nawabs of Lucknow and served with ulte tawe ka paratha.

uttar-pradesh.name: Awadhi Biryani
uttar-pradesh.blurb: Fragrant pulao-style biryani in which rice and mutton are cooked separately in stock, then layered and finished on dum in Lucknow's kitchens.

uttar-pradesh.name: Kachori Sabzi
uttar-pradesh.blurb: Crisp lentil-stuffed kachoris served with spicy potato curry and jalebi, the morning meal in the lanes leading down to Varanasi's ghats.

uttar-pradesh.name: Agra Petha
uttar-pradesh.blurb: Translucent candied cubes of ash gourd soaked in sugar syrup, sold in dozens of flavours in shops near the Taj Mahal.

uttar-pradesh.name: Mathura Peda
uttar-pradesh.blurb: Brown pedas made from milk reduced until caramelised and rolled in sugar, offered to Krishna in Mathura and Vrindavan temples.

uttarakhand.name: Kafuli
uttarakhand.blurb: Spinach and fenugreek greens cooked into a thick gravy with rice paste, a Garhwali dish eaten with rice or mandua roti.

uttarakhand.name: Bhatt ki Churkani
uttarakhand.blurb: Black soybeans from the hills cooked with iron-pan roasted spices and rice paste, a hearty Kumaoni dal.

uttarakhand.name: Aloo ke Gutke
uttarakhand.blurb: Boiled hill potatoes stir-fried with jakhiya seeds, red chilli and coriander, a simple Kumaoni snack served with tea or raita.

uttarakhand.name: Mandua ki Roti
uttarakhand.blurb: Flatbread of finger millet flour, dark and earthy, eaten with ghee and greens in mountain villages through the cold months.

uttarakhand.name: Bal Mithai
uttarakhand.blurb: Fudge of roasted khoya coated in tiny white sugar balls, a sweet from Almora sold across Kumaon.

west-bengal.name: Shorshe Ilish
west-bengal.blurb: Hilsa steaks cooked in a sharp mustard seed paste with green chillies and mustard oil, the most prized fish dish of the monsoon in Kolkata homes.

west-bengal.name: Kosha Mangsho
west-bengal.blurb: Mutton slow-fried with onions, ginger and spices until dark and dry, eaten with luchi or rice on Sunday afternoons and during Durga Puja.

west-bengal.name: Puchka
west-bengal.blurb: Crisp hollow puris filled with spiced mashed potato and dunked in tamarind water, Kolkata's version of pani puri sold on every street corner.

west-bengal.name: Luchi with Cholar Dal
west-bengal.blurb: Puffed deep-fried white-flour breads served with Bengal gram dal cooked with coconut and a touch of sugar, a festive breakfast.

west-bengal.name: Rosogolla
west-bengal.blurb: Spongy balls of fresh chhena simmered in light sugar syrup, a Bengali sweet made famous by Kolkata's confectioners.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Andaman Fish Curry
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.blurb: Fresh reef fish cooked in coconut milk with tamarind, chilli and curry leaves, eaten with rice in homes and eateries around Port Blair.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Grilled Lobster
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.blurb: Whole lobster grilled with garlic butter or a chilli masala, served at beach shacks on Havelock (Swaraj Dweep) and Neil Island.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Chilli Crab
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.blurb: Mud crabs from the mangroves stir-fried in a spicy tomato and chilli sauce, a popular seafood dish in Port Blair's restaurants.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Sambar Rice Meals
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.blurb: Rice served with sambar, rasam and vegetable poriyal on a banana leaf, brought by the islands' large Tamil and Telugu settler communities.

andaman-and-nicobar-islands.name: Coconut Ladoo
andaman-and-nicobar-islands.blurb: Grated island coconut cooked with jaggery or condensed milk and cardamom and rolled into balls, made in homes for festivals.

chandigarh.name: Chole Bhature
chandigarh.blurb: Spiced chickpea curry served with large puffed fried breads, a weekend breakfast staple in Chandigarh's sector markets.

chandigarh.name: Paneer Tikka
chandigarh.blurb: Cubes of paneer, onion and capsicum marinated in spiced yogurt and charred in a tandoor, a fixture on every Chandigarh dhaba menu.

chandigarh.name: Aloo Paratha with White Butter
chandigarh.blurb: Whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato, cooked on a griddle and topped with homemade white butter, often eaten with curd and pickle.

chandigarh.name: Tandoori Chicken
chandigarh.blurb: Chicken marinated in yogurt, red chilli and spices and roasted in a clay oven, a Punjabi favourite in the city's restaurants.

chandigarh.name: Gajar ka Halwa
chandigarh.blurb: Grated red winter carrots slow-cooked in milk, ghee and sugar with nuts, a cold-season sweet sold at sweet shops across the city.

dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.name: Pomfret Recheado
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.blurb: Pomfret slit and stuffed with a red Portuguese-style chilli, garlic and vinegar paste, then shallow-fried, served in Daman's seaside eateries.

dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.name: Bombil Fry
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.blurb: Bombay duck coated in semolina and spices and fried crisp, a common coastal catch on menus in Daman and Diu.

dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.name: Ubadiyu
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.blurb: Surti papdi beans, small potatoes and yam packed with herbs into an earthen pot and roasted upside down over a fire, a South Gujarat winter dish eaten across the region.

dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.name: Nagli Rotla
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.blurb: Thick finger millet flatbread eaten by the Warli and Kokna tribal communities of Dadra and Nagar Haveli with seasonal vegetables and chutney.

dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.name: Dodol
dadra-and-nagar-haveli-and-daman-and-diu.blurb: A dense, dark sweet of rice flour, coconut milk and jaggery stirred for hours, made by Daman's Catholic families at Christmas.

delhi.name: Butter Chicken
delhi.blurb: Tandoori chicken simmered in a mild tomato, butter and cream gravy, a dish created at Moti Mahal in Daryaganj and now eaten across the city.

delhi.name: Nihari
delhi.blurb: Slow-cooked mutton shank stew thickened with flour and spices, eaten with khameeri roti for breakfast near Jama Masjid.

delhi.name: Paranthe Wali Gali Parathas
delhi.blurb: Stuffed parathas fried in ghee with fillings like potato, paneer or rabri, served with chutneys in the narrow lane off Chandni Chowk.

delhi.name: Chole Kulche
delhi.blurb: Spicy white peas topped with onion, lemon and chutney and served with soft kulchas, sold from carts all over the city.

delhi.name: Daulat ki Chaat
delhi.blurb: Milk and cream whipped overnight into a light froth and topped with saffron and pistachio, sold in Old Delhi's lanes only during winter.

jammu-and-kashmir.name: Rogan Josh
jammu-and-kashmir.blurb: Mutton braised with Kashmiri red chillies, fennel and dry ginger in a rich red gravy, a centrepiece of the Kashmiri wazwan feast.

jammu-and-kashmir.name: Gushtaba
jammu-and-kashmir.blurb: Large pounded mutton balls simmered in a spiced yogurt gravy, traditionally the final dish served at a wazwan.

jammu-and-kashmir.name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
jammu-and-kashmir.blurb: Small potatoes fried and slow-cooked in a yogurt gravy with fennel, ginger powder and Kashmiri chilli, a Kashmiri Pandit favourite.

jammu-and-kashmir.name: Kalari Kulcha
jammu-and-kashmir.blurb: Kalari, a stretchy cheese from Udhampur, fried until crisp outside and tucked into a kulcha, a popular Jammu street snack.

jammu-and-kashmir.name: Phirni
jammu-and-kashmir.blurb: Ground rice cooked in milk with sugar and cardamom, set in small earthen bowls and topped with nuts, sold in Srinagar especially during Ramzan and Eid.

ladakh.name: Thukpa
ladakh.blurb: A noodle soup of hand-made noodles in mutton or vegetable broth with vegetables, eaten across Leh to warm up in the high-altitude cold.

ladakh.name: Skyu
ladakh.blurb: Thumb-pressed wheat dough pieces cooked in a stew with root vegetables and water, a hearty traditional Ladakhi home dish.

ladakh.name: Chutagi
ladakh.blurb: Bow-tie shaped wheat dough cooked with vegetables in a thick stock, a staple meal in Ladakhi homes during winter.

ladakh.name: Mok Mok
ladakh.blurb: Ladakhi momos filled with mutton or vegetables and served with chilli sauce and soup in the cafes of Leh market.

ladakh.name: Khambir with Butter Tea
ladakh.blurb: Thick, round local brown bread eaten for breakfast with gur gur cha, a salty tea churned with yak butter.

lakshadweep.name: Mas Curry
lakshadweep.blurb: Fresh tuna cooked in a coconut gravy with chilli, turmeric and curry leaves, the everyday main meal of the islands eaten with rice.

lakshadweep.name: Mas Podi
lakshadweep.blurb: Tuna boiled, smoked and sun-dried into hard pieces, then shredded and fried with onion, coconut and chilli, the islands' signature preserved fish.

lakshadweep.name: Octopus Fry
lakshadweep.blurb: Octopus caught from the lagoons cleaned, cut and fried with a coconut, chilli and pepper masala, a dish found on Kavaratti and Agatti.

lakshadweep.name: Tuna Cutlet
lakshadweep.blurb: Shredded tuna mixed with potato, onion and green chilli, crumbed and fried, served as a teatime snack in island homes.

lakshadweep.name: Kalathappam
lakshadweep.blurb: A dense rice-flour and jaggery cake cooked in a pot with coconut slivers and shallots fried in ghee, a Malabar-influenced sweet served with tea.

puducherry.name: Creole Fish Curry
puducherry.blurb: Fish cooked with coconut milk, tamarind and a French-Tamil spice blend, a dish of Pondicherry's Franco-Tamil Creole families.

puducherry.name: Prawn Assad
puducherry.blurb: Prawns simmered in a mild coconut milk gravy with ginger, garlic and turmeric, a classic of Pondicherry Creole home cooking.

puducherry.name: Meen Puttu
puducherry.blurb: Boiled fish crumbled and stir-fried with onions, garlic, curry leaves and spices, a coastal Tamil dish eaten with rice.

puducherry.name: Ven Pongal
puducherry.blurb: Rice and moong dal cooked soft with ghee, black pepper, cumin and cashews, served for breakfast with sambar and chutney in town eateries.

puducherry.name: Sundal
puducherry.blurb: Boiled chickpeas tempered with mustard seeds, curry leaves and grated coconut, sold in paper cones along the Promenade on Beach Road in the evening.
